messages:
incident-bot: P0: capacity-tier misrouting detected — several hosted tenant requests are appearing in Dedicated eu-central-1 pools. Auto-page triggered.

sara: pinging infra oncall. seeing error spikes and tenant isolation alarms. @oncall-infra are you awake?

oncall-infra: awake, looking. starting with routing traces and pool attach logs.

lee: initial signal: routing-service v3.14 rolled 00:04 ago; local test flagged no issues. logs show fallback path for 'hosted-standard' ends up selecting dedicated-reserved sets because of rule precedence bug.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: detected config-change: routing-map.json updated by lee. commit: 0a9f3b.

dina: showing cross-tenant cache collisions in dedicated caches — keys with prefix tenant:hosted:* present in dedicated namespace. KV read latency up.

carter-cs: customer ops reporting increased tail latency for a handful of hosted customers in EU. Opening tickets.

lee: root cause preview: an ordered-match rule in routing-map uses longest-prefix logic, but a new rule `service=hosted,region=eu-central` was accidentally added to the reserved-dedicated stanza. Should've been guarded with `tier==dedicated`. So hosted traffic matched reserved-dedicated first.

sara: what are mitigation options? rollback? patch? emergency ACL?

oncall-infra: rollback service deploy is safest but takes ~6-10m with canary. We can also push an emergency ACL to routing-proxy to block hosted->dedicated for eu-central which is ~45s to propagate. I'm leaning ACL + rollback.

ops-lead: do ACL + rollback. prioritize minimal blast radius.

lee: applying emergency ACL: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane.internal/acl/block -d '{"src_tier":"hosted","dst_pool":"dedicated-reserved","region":"eu-central"}'` -> submitted.

deploy-bot: ACL change accepted and propagated to edge proxies by deploy-bot. change_id: acl-1977-eu.

incident-bot: ALERT: after ACL, detected drop in cross-tenant KV hits in dedicated pools. Dedicated util falling.

oncall-infra: starting rollback of routing-service v3.14 to v3.13 canary in eu-central. staging canary healthy, rolling to 10% now.

dina: KV namespace scan in dedicated pools shows ~1200 keys written by hosted tenants. I'm starting eviction script to scrub ephemeral keys. Script: `python evict_cross_tenant.py --namespace dedicated-kv --marker hosted:`

carter-cs: customers notified with templated message. asking anyone who saw errors to add diagnostics.

lee: found the erroneous diff fragment:

```diff
-    - match: {service: hosted}
-      route: hosted-pool
+    - match: {service: hosted, region: eu-central}
+      route: dedicated-reserved
```

expected behaviour was to route hosted -> hosted-pool unless explicit tier dedicated.

ops-lead: were any model variants wrong (e.g., dedicated running a smaller quantized model vs hosted) that could cause correctness issues?

dina: dedicated-reserved runs larger-provisioned variants; we saw latency but no model-variant mismatches leading to wrong outputs. No integrity errors.

oncall-infra: rollback to v3.13 completed at +4:10. ACL remains until we validate no residual routing.

incident-bot: METRICS: dedicated eu-central cross-tenant reads dropped to baseline within 3m of rollback.

carter-cs: two customers (eu-host-21, eu-host-47) flagged spikes. Both acknowledged fix and asked for postmortem.

lee: immediate fixes: 1) revert the bad rule (PR opened), 2) add matcher schema validation preventing match rules that include region without tier constraints, 3) add canary test that simulates 1k hosted requests and asserts none land in dedicated pools.

ops-lead: longer term: add guardrail that limits hosted->dedicated spillover to max 0.5% per region, and introduce an automatic circuit-breaker that flips routing to safe-mode if cross-tenant KV hits > 0 for any dedicated pool.

dina: follow-up ops: KV eviction completed, wrote audit log: evict-197777. No evidence of data exfiltration. Evicted keys were ephemeral inference caches.

oncall-infra: leaving monitoring on. I'll hand off to evening oncall in 40m.

incident-bot: POST-INCIDENT: severity downgraded to P2. Postmortem owner: lee. Runbook ticket: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1977770007-runbook.

carter-cs: customer comms sent. Offering credits for measurable SLA breaches.

ops-lead: timeline for exec summary: detection 0:00, acl applied +1:20, rollback complete +4:10, dedicated KV scrub done +9:00. Impact: latency spikes for ~5-9 minutes for several hosted tenants in eu-central; KV cache contamination observed in dedicated pools but scrubbed; no data loss.

sara: thanks everyone. keep the thread alive for two hours for confirmation. I'll schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow 11:00 CET.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: please file postmortem within 48 hours.
